solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Your rent is included. That's saving money

indicators.note: the clue says the rent sits within the 'your' word, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: thy is the old form of your
a rent is a tear or split, a rift

explanation.surface: A tenant is told the rent is all-inclusive, which counts as a money-saver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord; here it is a tear, and 'is included' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being careful with spending, economical, is the adjective's ordinary sense.

clue.text: Having gone up before, it's liable to go up again

definitions.text: it's liable to go up again

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word for before is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, as in ante-room

explanation.surface: Something that has already erupted once may well blow again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having gone up' reverses ANTE in this down entry. 'Go up again' in the definition means erupt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano has erupted many times and is expected to blow its top again.

clue.text: People crack under intimidation

indicators.note: in a down entry, the crack word sits below the people word

parts.note: men are people
a crack shot is an ace, an expert

explanation.surface: People cave in when they are bullied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack under' looks like breaking under pressure, but 'crack' is ACE and 'under' places it beneath MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat or menacing behaviour is a form of intimidation, so the noun matches.

clue.text: Furious look given by whatsit

parts.note: to look is to see
a whatsit is an unnamed thing

explanation.surface: Someone gets an angry glare from a person whose name they cannot recall.
explanation.definitionFit: Boiling with suppressed anger is the figurative sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Wild tigers lurking in grass made an impression

indicators.note: the tigers are hiding inside the grass word, so they go within it

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

indicators.note: wild signals the tigers are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Wild tigers hiding in long grass left their mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' signals the anagram of the big cats, giving GISTER; 'lurking in' places it within the grass word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that registers makes an impression or sinks in; the past tense matches.

clue.text: Afraid wages cut will go through

indicators.note: the cut passes through the wages word, ending up inside it

parts.note: wages are pay
a nick is a small cut

explanation.surface: Workers fear that a pay cut is about to be pushed through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will go through' sounds like a policy being approved; here it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Panicky describes someone gripped by fear, close to afraid in sense.

clue.text: Break or make the star

indicators.note: to make something of letters is to form them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A choice between ruining someone and turning them into a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make or break' is a set phrase; 'make' is the anagram signal for THE STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To shatter is to break into pieces, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Cut to a lake, showing divers

parts.note: to sever is to cut
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Underwater swimmers are shown being cut off at a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' looks like people who dive; here it is the old adjective meaning various.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adjective means sundry or a number of, the same as more than a few.

clue.text: 'I will get home — I'm not incapable.' Priceless!

parts.note: a nest is a home
taken as written
not incapable means able

explanation.surface: A tipsy reveller insists they can get home fine, which is hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Priceless!' also suggests something comically absurd, matching the surface joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond valuing is literally priceless, too precious to put a figure on.

clue.text: Having a lot in common, attempt to win over

definitions.text: Having a lot in common, attempt to win over

parts.words: Having a lot in common, attempt to win over
parts.note: at an auction two people wanting the same lot try to outdo each other's offers

explanation.surface: Sounds like advice on persuading someone you share interests with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot in common' looks like shared interests, but it is an auction lot both people want.
explanation.definitionFit: Making competing offers for one item at a sale is exactly what this phrase describes.

clue.text: Girl in colourful band viewer really needs to see

definitions.text: colourful band viewer really needs to see
definitions.meaning: the coloured ring of the eye that controls the light let in

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a woman's given name and the coloured part of the eye around the pupil.

clue.text: They pull up corks

definitions.meaning: things or people that bring something to a halt
bungs put in the necks of bottles

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both things that halt something and the plugs that seal bottles.

clue.text: Pickle's lovely — hand over

parts.note: pretty means lovely
to pass something is to hand it over

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to pass the lovely pickle at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickle' looks like a condiment; here it means a predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe an awkward predicament or mess one has got into.

clue.text: Let through misprint — a keen reader might spot 'absorption'

indicators.note: the letters are passed through from the clue text as they stand
a sharp-eyed reader will see the word sitting inside the printed words

explanation.surface: A proofreader lets a typo pass that a keen reader would notice.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'misprINT — A KEen'; the misprint talk is a nod to the device.
explanation.definitionFit: The amount taken in or the act of taking something in is a synonym of absorption.

clue.text: They'll set tongues wagging!

parts.note: the tongue of a bell is its clapper, swung by those pulling the ropes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Set tongues wagging' suggests gossip; the tongues are bell clappers.
explanation.definitionFit: Campanologists swing church bells, making the clapper inside each one move.

clue.text: Cuts one dead in front of my boss. That's out of line

indicators.note: in a down entry these pieces come above the boss word

parts.note: to lop is to cut
I is the Roman numeral one
for a journalist, the boss is the editor, ED

explanation.surface: An employee snubs a colleague in view of the boss, which is unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts one dead' is an idiom for snubbing; it splits into LOPS, I and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Askew or uneven, leaning to one side, is a crooked state that is not aligned.

clue.text: Ticket with permit to get back in to see drawings

indicators.note: the reversed permit sits within the ticket word

parts.note: a pass is a ticket for entry

indicators.note: back means the word for permit is read in reverse

parts.note: to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A visitor needs a ticket and a permit to get back in to view an art show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To get back' turns the permit word round to TEL, and 'in' places it in the ticket word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pictures made with chalky coloured crayons are drawings of that kind.

clue.text: 'In sickness or…' Till death and beyond?

indicators.note: the word or goes in the sickness word

parts.note: a fever is a sickness

explanation.surface: Quoting marriage vows, wondering whether they last past death.
explanation.walkthrough: The vow fragment begs completion as 'in health', but 'In' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternally, for all time, goes past the end of life, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Dope linked to 'friend' over computer

indicators.note: over means the joined words are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis, dope
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A drug link to a so-called friend is found on someone's computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable personal computer for use on the knees is the item meant.

clue.text: Sweet tart? Decline!

parts.note: tart means sour, acid
to decline is to drop

explanation.surface: Someone is offered a sharp sweet and says no thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: An acid drop is a sharp-tasting British boiled sweet. 'Tart' looks like a pastry or a noun; here it is sour.
explanation.definitionFit: The confection is a hard boiled candy, so a sweet in British usage.

clue.text: Occupying hospital bed, private

parts.note: in means occupying, present inside
a ward is the room of hospital beds

explanation.surface: A patient is in a private hospital bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like a kind of hospital bed; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner, personal thoughts are kept to oneself, which is the private sense.

clue.text: Tantrums back stage

indicators.note: back means the tantrums word is read in reverse

parts.note: pets are fits of sulking, tantrums

explanation.surface: Divas throwing fits backstage.
explanation.definitionFit: A phase or step in a process is a stage, a synonym.

clue.text: On the rocks but unable to dive?

definitions.meaning: in trouble, especially short of money
where the sea is shallow, a diver cannot go in

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means hard up, and literally describes shallow water too low for diving.

clue.text: I heard he dropped round wanting a drink

indicators.note: dropped means the word he is taken out of the pool
round signals the remaining letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hears that a visitor called by and wanted a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropped round' looks like visiting; 'dropped' removes a pronoun leaving IARD, which 'round' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Parched, very dry, describes someone or somewhere in need of water.

clue.text: Had row about figure drawn from bank

indicators.note: the bank word goes about, around, the figure

parts.note: money drawn from a bank is cashed
L is the Roman numeral fifty, a figure

explanation.surface: An argument broke out over a sum withdrawn from the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue noisily or come into conflict is to have a row.

clue.text: Looking back, I would fall between study and skill being educated

indicators.note: the whole assembly is read from right to left
the letter falls into the gap between the two words

parts.note: a den is a study
art is skill

explanation.surface: Someone recalls falling between study and practical skill during schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: The assembly reads DENIART, which 'Looking back' reverses; 'would fall between' places the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Taught or schooled describes someone who has received instruction.
